PMF.IsCoupling: A joint law on A × B is a coupling of p and q if its first marginal is p and its second marginal is q.
PMF.isCoupling_channelJoint_const: Draw a point from p and draw a second point independently from q. The law of the resulting pair is a coupling of p and q.
PMF.exists_isCoupling: Any two discrete probability laws p and q admit a coupling, possibly on different alphabets.
PMF.isCoupling_map_diag: If X has law p, the law of (X,X) is a coupling of p with itself.
PMF.IsCoupling.map_swap: If the law of (X,Y) couples p and q, the law of (Y,X) couples q and p.
PMF.IsCoupling.map: If (X,Y) couples p and q, then (f(X),g(Y)) couples the pushforward of p by f with the pushforward of q by g.
PMF.IsCoupling.bind: Let (X,Y) couple p and q. Suppose that at every pair (x,y) of positive joint mass, the channel K(x,y) couples W(x) and V(y). Sampling from K(X,Y) then couples the output of p through W with the output of q through V.
PMF.IsCoupling.totalVariation_le: For any coupling (X,Y) of laws p and q on the same finite alphabet, TV(p,q) ≤ Pr[X ≠ Y].
PMF.maximalCoupling: For finite laws p and q, put s(x) = min(p(x),q(x)) and d = TV(p,q). Assign s(x) to each diagonal pair (x,x). If d > 0, distribute the remaining mass d by drawing the two coordinates independently from the normalized residual laws (p−s)/d and (q−s)/d. If d = 0, the construction consists only of the diagonal law.
PMF.isCoupling_maximalCoupling: The maximal coupling constructed from the finite laws p and q has first marginal p and second marginal q.
PMF.maximalCoupling_toOuterMeasure_ne: For the maximal coupling of p and q, the probability assigned to unequal pairs is the total variation distance TV(p,q), expressed as an extended nonnegative number.
PMF.maximalCoupling_toOuterMeasure_ne_to: For the maximal coupling of p and q, the real probability of unequal outcomes is exactly TV(p,q).
